entities.name: Adelaide, Abbess of Vilich
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Adelaide of Vilich (c. 960–1015) was the founding abbess of the Convent of Vilich near Bonn and is venerated as a saint in both the Catholic and Orthodox traditions. Born into the Swabian nobility, she was educated at the convents of Gernrode and Cologne and eventually founded the Convent of Vilich with her family's support around 978.

Vilich was part of the remarkable wave of Ottonian imperial women's monasticism — the 'Kanonissenstifter' (canonesses' foundations) and Benedictine convents that the Ottonian imperial family and their aristocratic allies founded across Germany in the tenth century. These foundations served simultaneously as centres of prayer, learning, and aristocratic family piety, and their abbesses were typically women of noble birth who combined genuine spirituality with administrative skill.

Adelaide's sister Bertrada founded another convent, and the two sisters represent the pattern of siblings collaborating in religious foundations that was common in Ottonian aristocratic culture. Adelaide also served as the director of the cathedral school at Cologne for a period, demonstrating the educational role that learned abbesses played in the Ottonian world. She is venerated on 5 February.
